links.reason: Line 2 (விடுவினை புடைக்கப் பாறி) ties parting to deeds, while Naladiyar 30 only says kin come unasked and go wordless (வாளாதே போவரால்); the verse never mentions death. The 'bird leaving the body' gain adds a decoration, not a cause or limit, and the epic's அத்தை is unsettled.
links.text_issue: line 3 அத்தை unfixed; sense flagged uncertain

links.reason: The Cintamani verse is two lines of an astrologer's words (மாதர்வாழ்வு மண்ணதே) and shows no king acting on them; Naladiyar 52's target is endless சத்தம் and சோதிடம் study set against death's urgency. A tension needs the verse to affirm astrology's truth as a rival doctrine, which it does not.

Kural 568's fault is a king who takes no counsel (இனத்தாற்றி எண்ணாத) and then rages; verse 37 shows only the king raging (வெகுண்டு) and ministers who quietly turn to another plan (மற்றொன்று செய்கின்றார்), so counsel was not 'heard and overridden' in the Tamil and anger does not 'rule the outcome'. The gain that anger leads to a plot is not a limit the couplet lacks.

Both make desire a fire (காம நீரெரி அகத்து கனன்று vs. அழல்... மனத்தைச் சுடுதலால் காமம்), but the epic verse is a body-description of hair-lines (தூம லேகைகள்) and the image of desire as fire is stock. Pairing adds little beyond the shared figure.

The nine openings and skin cover (ஒன்பது வாயில், தோலைப் போர்த்து / ஒன்பது வாய்ப்புலனும்... கருந்தோல்) are really shared, but the verse is addressed to Civakan's own heart (நெஞ்சு) and shows no woman before him, so 'a speaker, a woman and a test' and 'will still take wives, so disgust is a tool, not a rule' are not in the Tamil. 'Qualifies' is not earned.

Verse 636 is a narrator's hyperbole (காணார் போலும், 'it seems') about onlookers, and verse 29 says Civakan no longer wants women's pleasure; the two do not make incompatible claims, the ending simply fulfils or ironizes the hyperbole. So it is a qualification or foreshadowing, not a tension.

Pattinathar's verse is obscure (the needle, தீதற்ற மன்னவன் சிந்தை) and the note's 'sign from Siva' and 'ground is death' are readings the marker itself flags; the epic verse is a patikam summary of Civakan's bliss. Both turn from women (கொங்கை... கலவி / முலை போகம் வேண்டான்), but the contrast built on it is unsupported.

Both verses speak of earth and heaven (மண்முழுதன்றி வானும்... தந்தாய் / வையகமும் வானகமும் ஆற்றல் அரிது) and the king answers by giving his daughter (பாவை நின்பாலள்), which is a real case of acting on an unpayable debt. But the king says he finds no requital (கைம்மாறு காணேன்); that he accepts the couplet's verdict, or that Kural doctrine explains why he withholds wealth, is not in the Tamil.

Soolamani 52 does give a gentle-to-comers, hot-to-foes king (தண்ணியன் வெய்யன்), a real limit on any single ideal; but Kural 386 praises the land of a king easy of access and not harsh of speech, not the king, and nothing in it forbids heat to foes. 'Why approachability counts as praise' is not supplied by the epic.

2904 sends for the heir and 2912 has the king adorn a youth, which is story order with intervening verses; the marker notes 2912 does not say it is the same youth. Sequence is not a link, and 'the call is answered' rests on that unstated identity.

251 says no second authority rises under a king (மரத்தின்கீழ் ஆகா மரம்) and 253 warns that rivals on equal standing are like a snake in the room (பாம்போடு உடனுறையும்). They sit side by side in one chapter and 253's நிலைமையால் நேர்செய்து is ambiguous, so the pairing adds only a mild inference that the king keeps the ambitious below him.

Both name the same food of widowhood: ஆம்பல் அல்லி and the pond rice (குள நெல்) in the courtyard where Vijayai waits, and the widow's alli (அல்லிப் படுஉம் புல்) in Purananuru 248, a specific shared figure. The epic then turns it to the nursing doe and her son (நம்பியை நினைக்கும்), which the Sangam widow lacks, so both gains are specific.

21 is the patikam's summary and 1214 the full scene, so this is summary-to-detail inside one story rather than a fulfilment. The god in 1214 only says that meeting is his good fortune (குணம் அது); 21 adds the bow-sighting, so 'a political welcome as the fruit of foreknowledge' is read in, not stated.

38 lists three matters and does not say which they chose; 47 shows Udayana walking to the false elephant (கள்ள நல் யானை), so the link needs the verses between to know the plan is the lure. The claim that the lure is 'fitted to a king hunting for his elephant' is not in either verse; this is plot sequence.

1208 likens a straight road to chaste women's minds and 1212 a forking road to women's hearts, but the marker says மாற்றரு மணநெறி மகளிர் is doubtful, and the note's own teaches ends by saying no view of women is settled. A tension resting on an unsettled phrase, resolved to 'no tension', is forced.

Soolamani 4 claims the discerning in the king's assembly accepted the work (தெருண்டார் கொளப்பட்டதன்றே); Cintamani 6 says he set out to tell it to the discerning's assembly (தெருண்டார் அவை செப்பலுற்றேன்). Both are conventional prefatory gestures, and 'asks for approval' overreads செப்பலுற்றேன். Qualifies is too strong.

Verse 68 ranks the poor above those who hold wealth and only guard it (காப்பாரின் / வைத்தாரின் நல்லர் வறியவர்), which goes beyond Kural 228's rebuke of hoarders who keep and lose (வைத்திழக்கும் வன்கணவர்): kept wealth is placed below poverty, not merely below giving. The note describes both accurately.
links.text_issue: verse flagged uncertain in later lines

links.reason: Pairing rests on a queen's pique in each (ஊடல் in Sil 16.134 / Dattai's சீற்றம்) while the rest of the note imports events outside the units (Dattai's anger 'ends in worship', the sulk 'opens the way for the lie'). The marker says the Sil passage does not name the sulk as the cause. A shared domestic mood dressed as a contrast of consequences.

1627 crowns the groves as kings (அரசெனப் பட்டஞ் சேர்த்தி) and 1643 has the women win the grove (சோலையைக் காரிகையார் வென்றார்), a pleasant echo within one festival description, but it is story order, not a later verse answering an earlier. 'First a court then a thing conquered' is only wordplay.

The link needs the hero holding the mountain in 1517 to be the lord addressed in 273, which neither verse states, and 273's mountain is a hypothetical (வயிரக் குன்றம்... ஏந்தி) the counsellor sets against austerity and rule. 'Rule is what he must still carry' is a reconstructed plot.

2072 speaks of a road of meditation (தியான வீதி) to a world without return; Tirumanthiram 126 climbs the thirty-six tattvas as rungs (படிமுத்தி ஏணி). Neither says grace or effort, so the grace-versus-effort contrast is imported, and the 'couplet' in the gains is a verse. Shared 'climb by stages' is thin since 2072 gives no stages.

Both vows hinge on seeing the enemy's backs (புறக்கொடை கண்டு / அவர்ப்புறம் காணேன்) and name a forfeit, but Civakan's forfeit is his name and the prize a bride (முகிழ்முலை கலப்பலன்றேல்), while the Pandya's is parting from his wife (பிரிக). The note and both gains are accurate.

Both show a city's wealth lying untaken, but the epic verse is about scattered girdle beads that none cares to gather (கொள்ளும் நீரர் இன்மையின்) and the Sil passage about a court where thieves are made to whirl; calling these 'two theories of order' is over-built. A shared topos, different devices.

Adjacent verses in one report scene: spies tell the king (169) and then someone reports Udayanan's deed and the king is glad (170). The marker says even who does the telling in 170 is unclear. Sequence, not an answer or fulfilment.

Both put the lover's chest, marked by women's breasts, in the war scene (முலைகள்... உழ உவந்த மார்பம் / முலை பொருது சேந்த மார்பன்), but in 2273 who is meant is only inferred (Padumukan) and the figure is a stock heroic-erotic topos. 'Marks the victim and the victor' is a tidy symmetry, not a meaningful use.

797 says leaving fools' friendship is gain; 805 tells one to read a friend's hurt as folly or intimacy (பேதைமை ஒன்றோ பெருங்கிழமை). These address different cases, and 'the only difference is how old the bond is' is invented; 805 never says to 'go on'. Different advice for different situations is not a tension.

963 raises Arkakirti onto the king's young elephant (மழகளிறு எருத்த மேற்றினான்); 845 has him on an elephant (ஆனைமேல்) but does not say it is his own, so the 'replaced elephant' is read in. Same-chapter story order.

Kural 329 judges killing as a trade (கொலைவினையர்) as base; 1205 calls the forest bowmen 'sin in form' (பாவ மூர்த்தியர்) in a warning about the road. That the epic 'hardens the ethic into a view of hunters' and 'applies the principle to whole groups' is not in the Tamil, and the epic verse never invokes the couplet's reason.
links.text_issue: flag: line 1 possible lost vowel sign

links.reason: 103 has the friend relieved that the keeper's ugliness will end the queen's passion (கழுதுருவவன்... ஒழியுமென்று உவந்து) and 111 has her tell him the queen's desire (விழைவு சொன்னாள்), which is plot order. The Tamil never says the friend 'took the queen's side' and 111 does not show the idea failing; no incompatible claims.

Line 3-4 (கொல்லா விரதம் குடை மன்னவாமெனின் வெல்லா வகையில்லை) offers non-killing to kings as the way to conquest, a case Kural 325 (கொல்லாமை சூழ்வான் தலை among renouncers) does not foresee; the note renders both accurately. Lines 1-2 are hard, but the gains rest on lines 3-4.

1412 is the Suramai king's army thrown into confusion by the cry (அடங்கினன்... ஓவென), while 1414 is the young king's army that roars (வையமாளிளையவன் தானை); these are two armies, so 'the army's despair and its roar' is one force only by a reading. 1413 sits between; this is battle sequence.

Cintamani 232 compares a king left by Fortune to a wood-apple an elephant has swallowed (துற்றிய வெள்ளிலே போல்) and Tirumanthiram 2593 says Siva swallows soul and world like the elephant-eaten wood-apple (கரியுண் விளவின் கனி). The shared figure is distinctive and the shared use (outward form kept, inside taken) is meaningful, with ruin turned into absorption.
links.text_issue: 232 sense flagged uncertain; TM 2593 திரிய unclear

links.reason: 107 foretells a Vidyadhara king giving one daughter (தன்மகளொருத்தி தன்னைத் தந்தனன்); 408 is a different astrologer's compressed speech (ஒன்றுனக் கிரண்டு சேடியும்) whose sense the marker admits is a likely reading. Two prophecies of one match, one fulfilling the other as plot, is not 'agrees'.

Kural 1268's speaker is the man for Parimelazhagar and the woman for Manakkudavar, and the note picks the man's reading; Natrinai 374's wife (விருந்து அயர் விருப்பினள்) shares only the guest-feast word. 'Each partner ascribed the feast to the other' is conjecture, not a development.

Kural 1168 is about night (மன்னுயிர் எல்லாம் துயிற்றி) and has no companion but her, while Cintamani 1524 has no night in the verse; she is consoling her reflection (நிழல்... அழேல்). The 'night with no companion' frame is not in the epic's Tamil, so the gains and teaches are imported.

3132 shows penance piled up (நற்றவந் தாளினீட்டினார்) and 3134 their end on the mountain and rebirth as gods (தேவராயினார்), which is story order; the marker even says the group is read as ascetics only from the next verse. The ripening-into-heaven point is true but sits in 3134 alone.

476 has Nandagon draw back because of the banyan-seed hope (ஆலம்வித்தனைய தெண்ணி); 26 is the patikam summary of Civakan's just sceptre. Calling the hope 'the plan of the whole epic' overreads one servant's hope, and மால்வழி is unfixed. A prefigured hope and its summary fulfilment, thin.

Both turn on one scene: Suramanjari vows offerings to Kama for Civakan's chest (அகலஞ் சேர்தின்... வீவல்), and in 2062 he worships her as a goddess (தெய்வமென்றே... சீறடி பரவ வந்தேன்). The worship runs the other way, as the note says, though the 'one shrine' is the note's.

208 is Rudradattan's polemical slur on Siva's half-woman form (பாகம் கொண்டதே மறுவது ஆகப் பெரும்பழி) and Tirumanthiram 16 names that same god by it (மாது குலாவிய வாள்நுதல் பாகனை) as the one the gods delight in: an incompatible valuation of one thing. Both gains are true; the TM line is obscure but the epithet is not.

Padumai's loss of bloom and bangles after seeing Civakan (1291, நிறையும் நாணும் மாமையும்... வளையும்) is echoed by the city's women (2550, மாமை கைவளையொடு). That is a repeated motif, not a fulfilment; 'beauty unsettles a crowd' is the teaches' only gain and is a theme.

Both treat leaving for forest and wearing away deeds, but 1434's last line is hard (பறைக்குற்றாற் பறைக்கலாமே) and the 'knowledge supplied in 1436' is outside these units. Neelakesi 18 says forest-dwellers strive with knowledge (ஞானமொடு) and does not say that going alone fails, so 'qualifies' leans on the unseen verse.

237 answers 234-235 with breath and conch, but the verse does not name the weighing or the pit and lines 1-3 are corrupt per the marker; 'meets each of his tests by name' is untrue. A reply to a refuted claim is a real within-epic link, but the type is an answer, not a qualification.

Both are Jain hymns praising an omniscient lord (கேவலம் / காலமொரு மூன்றுணர்ந்த) who burns deeds (வெவ்வினை வீடு / தொல்வினையெல்லாமெரித்த), but they are opening praise in two poems, so 'the same act twice' is a shared convention, not a development of one by the other.
